sections.heading: Intro
sections.content_markdown: This layer is the AI's reference catalog for schedule-building, substitution logic, and user-facing explanations. Each entry follows the 15-field template defined in the Tier 2 briefing. Goal applicability uses Tier 1 codes (A1–G5).

entries.heading: 1. Back Squat
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Squat
**Primary**: Quadriceps · Glutes
**Secondary**: Adductors · Hamstrings · Erector spinae · Core
**Equipment**: Barbell, squat rack, plates. *Swaps*: front squat · goblet squat · safety bar squat · belt squat
**Unilateral**: No
**Difficulty**: Intermediate
**Tags**: compound · primary lift · strength · hypertrophy
**Form cues**:
Brace core before unracking
Sit between your hips, not behind them
Knees track over mid-foot
Hit depth, drive through full foot
Stand tall before re-racking
**Common errors**:
Knees caving inward (valgus collapse)
Heels lifting at depth (ankle mobility limit)
Excessive forward lean (often a quad-strength or ankle issue)
Loss of upper-back tightness (bar drifts)
Cutting depth (pelvis stays high)
**Substitution alternatives** *(ordered by similarity)*:
Front squat · safety bar squat · goblet squat · belt squat · Bulgarian split squat
**Pairing logic**: Pairs with hamstring-dominant work (RDL, hamstring curl), upper-body push or pull, core anti-rotation. Poor pair with heavy front squat or deadlift in same session (CNS conflict).
**Goal applicability**: Build muscle (A2) · Sustainable fat loss (A4) · General strength (B1) · Strength peak (B2) · Strength endurance (B3) · Hybrid athlete (C4) · Team sport season prep (off-season) (C9) · General health maintenance (D1) · Bone density (D4) · Mobility & joint health (D5) · Menopause-aware training (F5) · Senior fitness (F6) · Glute development (G1) · Athletic look (G3)
**Video URL**: *placeholder*
**Sources**: Schoenfeld, B. (2010). Squatting kinematics and kinetics and their application to exercise performance. J Strength Cond Res. · Hartmann, H. et al. (2013). Influence of squatting depth on jumping performance. J Strength Cond Res. · Rippetoe, M. Starting Strength (3rd ed., Aasgaard, 2011).

entries.heading: 2. Front Squat
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Squat
**Primary**: Quadriceps · Upper back (isometric)
**Secondary**: Glutes · Core · Adductors
**Equipment**: Barbell, squat rack, plates. *Swaps*: goblet squat · zercher squat · safety bar squat
**Unilateral**: No
**Difficulty**: Intermediate–Advanced (rack position demands wrist/shoulder mobility)
**Tags**: compound · primary lift · strength · hypertrophy · mobility-demanding
**Form cues**:
Elbows high throughout
Upper back stays tight
Sit between hips
Drive through full foot
Maintain rack position to lockout
**Common errors**:
Elbows dropping (bar collapses forward)
Excessive forward lean
Cutting depth
Letting upper back round
**Substitution alternatives**: Goblet squat · zercher squat · back squat · safety bar squat · belt squat
**Pairing logic**: Pairs with hamstring/glute work (RDL, hip thrust), upper-body work. Poor pair with overhead pressing same session (rack-position fatigue compounds).
**Goal applicability**: Build muscle (A2) · General strength (B1) · Strength peak (B2) · Hybrid athlete (C4) · General health maintenance (D1) · Mobility & joint health (D5) · Menopause-aware training (F5) · Athletic look (G3)
**Video URL**: *placeholder*
**Sources**: Gullett, J. et al. (2009). A biomechanical comparison of back and front squats in healthy trained individuals. J Strength Cond Res. · Yavuz, H. et al. (2015). Kinematic and EMG activities during front and back squat variations in maximum loads. J Sports Sci.

entries.heading: 3. Overhead Squat
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Squat
**Primary**: Quadriceps · Glutes · Shoulders (isometric)
**Secondary**: Core · Upper back · Adductors
**Equipment**: Barbell, plates. Optional rack. *Swaps*: dumbbell overhead squat · single-arm overhead squat · front squat (when overhead is contraindicated)
**Unilateral**: No
**Difficulty**: Advanced (mobility + stability demands)
**Tags**: compound · accessory · mobility-demanding · skill
**Form cues**:
Lock arms overhead
Bar over mid-foot
Sit straight down
Maintain shoulder position throughout
Feet flat
**Common errors**:
Bar drifting forward (shoulder mobility limit)
Losing lockout
Forward lean
Ankle restriction limiting depth
**Substitution alternatives**: Dumbbell overhead squat · front squat · goblet squat with overhead reach · back squat
**Pairing logic**: Useful as warm-up or low-load skill work. Poor as fatigued accessory (form degrades fast).
**Goal applicability**: General strength (B1) · Strength endurance (B3) · Hybrid athlete (C4) · Climbing/bouldering (C8) · Mobility & joint health (D5)
**Video URL**: *placeholder*
**Sources**: Donnelly, D. et al. (2006). The effect of overhead squat performance on vertical jump performance. J Strength Cond Res. · Lorenzetti, S. et al. (2018). Comparison of the angles and corresponding moments in the knee and hip during restricted and unrestricted squats. BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil.

entries.heading: 4. Box Squat
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Squat
**Primary**: Quadriceps · Glutes · Hamstrings
**Secondary**: Adductors · Erector spinae · Core
**Equipment**: Barbell, squat rack, plates, plyo box or bench at squat depth. *Swaps*: pause squat (no box) · pin squat (rack pins at depth)
**Unilateral**: No
**Difficulty**: Intermediate
**Tags**: compound · accessory · strength · technique
**Form cues**:
Sit back to box (don't squat down to it)
Pause briefly
Drive up through full foot
Stay tight on box
Don't relax torso
**Common errors**:
Crashing onto box (no eccentric control)
Rocking forward off box
Losing back tightness during pause
Overshooting depth
**Substitution alternatives**: Pause squat · pin squat · back squat · front squat
**Pairing logic**: Excellent paired with hamstring/posterior work. Pairs with upper body work. Less ideal stacked with heavy back squats.
**Goal applicability**: General strength (B1) · Strength peak (B2) · Strength endurance (B3) · Team sport season prep (C9)
**Video URL**: *placeholder*
**Sources**: McBride, J. et al. (2010). Comparison of kinetic variables and muscle activity during a squat vs. a box squat. J Strength Cond Res. · Tate, D. Westside Barbell Book of Methods (Westside Barbell, 2008).

entries.heading: 5. Conventional Deadlift
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Hinge
**Primary**: Glutes · Hamstrings · Erector spinae
**Secondary**: Quadriceps · Trapezius · Lats · Forearms (grip)
**Equipment**: Barbell, plates (preferably bumper or competition-style for full ROM). *Swaps*: trap bar deadlift · sumo deadlift · Romanian deadlift
**Unilateral**: No
**Difficulty**: Intermediate–Advanced
**Tags**: compound · primary lift · strength · power
**Form cues**:
Bar over mid-foot
Shoulders slightly ahead of bar at start
Take slack out of bar
Drive floor away
Stand tall, lockout at hips
**Common errors**:
Bar drifting forward of mid-foot
Rounding lower back at start
Hyperextending at lockout
Pulling with arms
Jerking start (no slack pull)
**Substitution alternatives**: Trap bar deadlift · sumo deadlift · block pull · Romanian deadlift
**Pairing logic**: Pairs with upper-body push/pull (different system). Poor pair with heavy squat same session (CNS + low back fatigue). Poor finisher (form fades under fatigue).
**Goal applicability**: Build muscle (A2) · Body recomposition (A3) · General strength (B1) · Strength peak (B2) · Strength endurance (B3) · Team sport season prep (off-season) (C9) · General health maintenance (D1) · Bone density (D4) · Menopause-aware training (F5) · Senior fitness (F6) · Glute development (G1) · Athletic look (G3)
**Video URL**: *placeholder*
**Sources**: Escamilla, R. et al. (2000). A three-dimensional biomechanical analysis of sumo and conventional style deadlifts. Med Sci Sports Exerc. · Hales, M. (2010). Improving the deadlift: understanding biomechanical constraints and physiological adaptations to resistance exercise. Strength Cond J. · Rippetoe, M. Starting Strength (3rd ed., 2011).

entries.heading: 6. Sumo Deadlift
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Hinge
**Primary**: Glutes · Quadriceps · Adductors
**Secondary**: Hamstrings · Erector spinae · Trapezius · Forearms
**Equipment**: Barbell, plates. *Swaps*: conventional deadlift · trap bar deadlift · wide-stance Romanian deadlift
**Unilateral**: No
**Difficulty**: Intermediate–Advanced
**Tags**: compound · primary lift · strength
**Form cues**:
Wide stance, toes turned out
Grip inside legs
Chest up
Push knees out as you set up
Drive floor away with feet
**Common errors**:
Stance too narrow (no leverage advantage)
Hips rising before bar (becomes RDL)
Knees caving inward
Rounding upper back
**Substitution alternatives**: Conventional deadlift · trap bar deadlift · wide-stance kettlebell deadlift
**Pairing logic**: Pairs with upper body and core. Poor stacked with conventional deadlift. Poor as finisher.
**Goal applicability**: Build muscle (A2) · General strength (B1) · Strength peak (B2) · Strength endurance (B3) · Menopause-aware training (F5)
**Video URL**: *placeholder*
**Sources**: Escamilla, R. et al. (2000). A three-dimensional biomechanical analysis of sumo and conventional style deadlifts. Med Sci Sports Exerc. · Belcher, D. (2017). The sumo deadlift. Strength Cond J.

entries.heading: 7. Romanian Deadlift (RDL)
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Hinge
**Primary**: Hamstrings · Glutes
**Secondary**: Erector spinae · Adductors · Forearms (grip)
**Equipment**: Barbell, plates. *Swaps*: dumbbell RDL · kettlebell RDL · single-leg RDL · cable RDL
**Unilateral**: No (single-leg version available)
**Difficulty**: Beginner–Intermediate
**Tags**: compound · accessory · hypertrophy · hamstring-dominant
**Form cues**:
Soft knees, don't bend more than start position
Push hips back
Bar stays close to legs
Feel hamstrings stretch
Stand tall, squeeze glutes at top
**Common errors**:
Squatting the movement (knees bend too much)
Rounding lower back at bottom
Letting bar drift forward
Over-extending at top
**Substitution alternatives**: Dumbbell RDL · single-leg RDL · cable pull-through · good morning · kettlebell deadlift
**Pairing logic**: Excellent in supersets with quad-dominant or upper body. Pairs with hip thrust as posterior chain duo. Poor finisher after heavy deadlift (overlapping stimulus).
**Goal applicability**: Get lean (A1) · Build muscle (A2) · Body recomposition (A3) · Sustainable fat loss (A4) · General strength (B1) · Strength endurance (B3) · Race prep, short distance (C1) · Race prep, long distance (C2) · Trail running (C3) · Hybrid athlete (C4) · Cycling event prep (C5) · Racquet sports (C7) · Team sport season prep (C9) · General health maintenance (D1) · Bone density (D4) · Mobility & joint health (D5) · Knee rehab (E1) · Hip rehab (E4) · Menopause-aware training (F5) · Senior fitness (F6) · Glute development (G1) · Athletic look (G3)
**Video URL**: *placeholder*
**Sources**: McAllister, M. et al. (2014). Muscle activation during various hamstring exercises. J Strength Cond Res. · Schoenfeld, B. Science and Development of Muscle Hypertrophy (Human Kinetics, 2nd ed. 2020). · Helms, Morgan, Valdez. The Muscle and Strength Pyramid: Training (2nd ed., 2019).

entries.heading: 8. Trap Bar Deadlift
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Hinge (squat-hinge hybrid)
**Primary**: Quadriceps · Glutes · Hamstrings
**Secondary**: Erector spinae · Trapezius · Forearms · Core
**Equipment**: Trap bar (hex bar), plates. *Swaps*: conventional deadlift · sumo deadlift · dumbbell deadlift
**Unilateral**: No
**Difficulty**: Beginner–Intermediate (more forgiving than conventional)
**Tags**: compound · primary lift · strength · power · beginner-friendly
**Form cues**:
Stand inside the trap bar, mid-foot under handles
Brace, take slack out
Push floor away
Stand tall
Control descent
**Common errors**:
Squatting too low at setup (becomes pure squat)
Rounding back
Not engaging lats
**Substitution alternatives**: Conventional deadlift · sumo deadlift · kettlebell deadlift · dumbbell deadlift
**Pairing logic**: Pairs well with most accessories given lower spinal load than conventional. Suitable as primary in general strength programs.
**Goal applicability**: Build muscle (A2) · General strength (B1) · Strength endurance (B3) · Team sport season prep (C9) · General health maintenance (D1) · Bone density (D4) · Lower back rehab (Phase 3) (E2) · Menopause-aware training (F5) · Senior fitness (F6)
**Video URL**: *placeholder*
**Sources**: Camara, K. et al. (2016). An examination of muscle activation and power characteristics while performing the deadlift exercise with straight and hexagonal barbells. J Strength Cond Res. · Swinton, P. et al. (2011). A biomechanical analysis of straight and hexagonal barbell deadlifts using submaximal loads. J Strength Cond Res.

entries.heading: 9. Bench Press
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Horizontal push
**Primary**: Pectoralis major · Anterior deltoid · Triceps
**Secondary**: Lats (stabilizer) · Core
**Equipment**: Barbell, bench, rack. *Swaps*: dumbbell bench press · machine chest press · push-up (for scaling) · floor press
**Unilateral**: No
**Difficulty**: Beginner–Intermediate
**Tags**: compound · primary lift · strength · hypertrophy
**Form cues**:
Feet planted firmly
Slight arch in upper back
Scapulae retracted and depressed
Bar to lower chest, slight angle
Drive feet into floor as you press
**Common errors**:
Flaring elbows out 90° (shoulder strain)
Bouncing bar off chest
Feet up or shifting
Uneven pressing (one side ahead)
**Substitution alternatives**: Dumbbell bench press · machine chest press · floor press · push-up variations
**Pairing logic**: Pairs with rowing variations (antagonist superset) or lower-body work. Poor stacked with heavy overhead pressing same session (shoulder fatigue).
**Goal applicability**: Build muscle (A2) · General strength (B1) · Strength peak (B2) · Team sport season prep (C9) · General health maintenance (D1) · Bone density (D4) · Menopause-aware training (F5) · Arm focus (G2) · Athletic look (G3)
**Video URL**: *placeholder*
**Sources**: Krzysztofik, M. et al. (2020). The effects of resistance training experience on the bench press throw. Int J Environ Res Public Health. · Madsen, N., McLaughlin, T. (1984). Kinematic factors influencing performance and injury risk in the bench press exercise. Med Sci Sports Exerc. · Rippetoe, M. Starting Strength (3rd ed., 2011).

entries.heading: 10. Incline Bench Press
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Horizontal push (with vertical bias)
**Primary**: Upper pectoralis · Anterior deltoid · Triceps
**Secondary**: Lats · Core
**Equipment**: Barbell, incline bench (~30°), rack. *Swaps*: incline dumbbell press · landmine press · low-incline machine press
**Unilateral**: No (single-arm DB version available)
**Difficulty**: Intermediate
**Tags**: compound · accessory · hypertrophy · upper-chest emphasis
**Form cues**:
Set bench to ~30° (steeper shifts to shoulders)
Same scapular position as bench
Bar to upper chest
Drive bar slightly back, not straight up
**Common errors**:
Incline too steep (becomes overhead press)
Pressing bar straight up
Flaring elbows
Losing scapular tightness
**Substitution alternatives**: Incline dumbbell press · machine incline press · landmine press · standing landmine press
**Pairing logic**: Pairs with row variations. Pairs with arm/shoulder isolation work. Pairs less well with overhead press same session.
**Goal applicability**: Build muscle (A2) · General strength (B1) · Hybrid athlete (C4) · Team sport season prep (C9) · General health maintenance (D1) · Menopause-aware training (F5) · Arm focus (G2) · Athletic look (G3)
**Video URL**: *placeholder*
**Sources**: Trebs, A. et al. (2010). An electromyographic analysis of 3 muscles surrounding the shoulder joint during the performance of a chest press exercise at several angles. J Strength Cond Res. · Lauver, J. et al. (2017). Influence of bench angle on upper extremity muscular activation during bench press exercise. Eur J Sport Sci.

entries.heading: 11. Close-Grip Bench Press
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Horizontal push
**Primary**: Triceps · Pectoralis (sternal head)
**Secondary**: Anterior deltoid · Core
**Equipment**: Barbell, bench, rack. *Swaps*: close-grip dumbbell press · diamond push-up · dip · floor press close grip
**Unilateral**: No
**Difficulty**: Beginner–Intermediate
**Tags**: compound · accessory · strength · triceps emphasis
**Form cues**:
Grip slightly inside shoulder width (not painfully narrow)
Elbows tucked toward ribs
Bar to lower chest
Drive elbows forward and up
**Common errors**:
Grip too narrow (wrist strain)
Elbows flaring (loses triceps emphasis)
Bar path too high on chest
**Substitution alternatives**: Close-grip dumbbell press · dip · floor press · diamond push-up
**Pairing logic**: Pairs with rowing or pulling work. Pairs with overhead triceps extension as triceps duo. Less ideal stacked with heavy regular bench.
**Goal applicability**: Build muscle (A2) · General strength (B1) · Strength peak (B2) · Strength endurance (B3) · Arm focus (G2)
**Video URL**: *placeholder*
**Sources**: Lehman, G. (2005). The influence of grip width and forearm pronation/supination on upper-body myoelectric activity during the flat bench press. J Strength Cond Res. · Saeterbakken, A. et al. (2017). Effects of bench press with and without weight chains on velocity and power output. J Strength Cond Res.

entries.heading: 12. Overhead Press (Standing Barbell)
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Vertical push
**Primary**: Anterior deltoid · Lateral deltoid · Triceps
**Secondary**: Core (anti-extension) · Upper chest · Trapezius
**Equipment**: Barbell, plates, rack. *Swaps*: standing dumbbell press · seated barbell press · seated dumbbell press · landmine press · machine shoulder press
**Unilateral**: No (single-arm DB version available)
**Difficulty**: Intermediate
**Tags**: compound · primary lift · strength · core
**Form cues**:
Bar in front of shoulders at start, elbows slightly forward
Brace core hard
Drive head through arms at lockout
Stay tall, no leaning back
Full lockout at top
**Common errors**:
Excessive lower back arch (becomes incline press standing)
Pressing bar around face instead of past
Elbows flared sideways
Partial lockout
**Substitution alternatives**: Seated barbell press · standing dumbbell press · seated dumbbell press · machine press
**Pairing logic**: Pairs with rowing or pulling. Poor stacked with heavy bench same session (shoulder fatigue). Poor as finisher (form degrades).
**Goal applicability**: Build muscle (A2) · General strength (B1) · Strength peak (B2) · Strength endurance (B3) · Team sport season prep (C9) · General health maintenance (D1) · Bone density (D4) · Menopause-aware training (F5) · Arm focus (G2) · Athletic look (G3)
**Video URL**: *placeholder*
**Sources**: Saeterbakken, A., Fimland, M. (2013). Effects of body position and loading modality on muscle activity and strength in shoulder presses. J Strength Cond Res. · Lauver, J. et al. (2017). Influence of bench angle on upper extremity muscular activation during bench press exercise. Eur J Sport Sci. · Rippetoe, M. Starting Strength (3rd ed., 2011).

entries.heading: 13. Push Press
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Vertical push (with leg drive)
**Primary**: Anterior deltoid · Lateral deltoid · Triceps · Quadriceps (drive)
**Secondary**: Core · Trapezius · Glutes
**Equipment**: Barbell, plates, rack. *Swaps*: dumbbell push press · single-arm push press · jerk (more advanced)
**Unilateral**: No
**Difficulty**: Intermediate
**Tags**: compound · accessory · power · explosive
**Form cues**:
Quarter dip with vertical torso
Drive feet into floor explosively
Transmit drive through bar
Arms finish overhead
Re-rack with control
**Common errors**:
Forward lean during dip
Dipping too deep (becomes thruster)
Disconnecting drive from press
Soft lockout
**Substitution alternatives**: Dumbbell push press · standing barbell press (without leg drive, scaled load) · single-arm push press · landmine push press
**Pairing logic**: Pairs with pulling work. Pairs with hybrid conditioning work. Poor stacked with heavy strict overhead press.
**Goal applicability**: Strength endurance (B3) · Hybrid athlete (C4) · Combat sports prep (C6) · Racquet sports (C7) · Team sport season prep (C9) · Youth athletics (F7)
**Video URL**: *placeholder*
**Sources**: Lake, J. et al. (2014). The effect of push press load on kinetic and kinematic indicators of lower body power. J Strength Cond Res. · Cormie, P. et al. (2007). The influence of body mass on calculation of power during lower-body resistance exercises. J Strength Cond Res.

entries.heading: 14. Barbell Row (Bent-Over Row)
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Horizontal pull
**Primary**: Lats · Rhomboids · Mid-trapezius · Posterior deltoid
**Secondary**: Biceps · Forearms · Erector spinae · Core
**Equipment**: Barbell, plates. *Swaps*: dumbbell row · pendlay row · t-bar row · seal row · chest-supported row
**Unilateral**: No (single-arm DB row is the unilateral variant)
**Difficulty**: Intermediate
**Tags**: compound · primary lift · strength · hypertrophy · back-dominant
**Form cues**:
Hinge at hips, torso ~45°
Soft knees
Bar at shins
Pull to lower ribs
Squeeze shoulder blades
Control descent
**Common errors**:
Standing too upright (loses lat emphasis)
Using momentum (becomes a swing)
Pulling with arms before back
Jerky tempo
Lower back rounding
**Substitution alternatives**: Pendlay row · t-bar row · chest-supported row · dumbbell row · seal row
**Pairing logic**: Pairs with bench press as antagonist superset. Pairs with vertical pull (different angle). Pairs less well stacked with heavy deadlifts (low back fatigue).
**Goal applicability**: Build muscle (A2) · General strength (B1) · Strength peak (B2) · Strength endurance (B3) · Team sport season prep (C9) · General health maintenance (D1) · Bone density (D4) · Menopause-aware training (F5) · Arm focus (G2) · Athletic look (G3)
**Video URL**: *placeholder*
**Sources**: Fenwick, C. et al. (2009). Comparison of different rowing exercises: trunk muscle activation and lumbar spine motion, load, and stiffness. J Strength Cond Res. · Lehman, G. et al. (2004). The importance of normalisation in the interpretation of surface electromyography. J Manipulative Physiol Ther.

entries.heading: 15. Pendlay Row
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Horizontal pull
**Primary**: Lats · Rhomboids · Mid-trapezius · Posterior deltoid
**Secondary**: Biceps · Erector spinae · Core
**Equipment**: Barbell, plates. *Swaps*: barbell row (continuous) · t-bar row · chest-supported row
**Unilateral**: No
**Difficulty**: Intermediate
**Tags**: compound · accessory · strength · explosive
**Form cues**:
Bar starts on floor each rep
Torso parallel to floor
Explosive pull to lower chest
Controlled return to floor (full reset)
Brace core throughout
**Common errors**:
Torso rising during pull (cheating)
Not resetting on floor (becomes barbell row)
Using momentum on first inch
**Substitution alternatives**: Barbell row · t-bar row · chest-supported row
**Pairing logic**: Pairs with horizontal push and core work. Poor stacked with deadlifts (low back). Works well in strength-endurance circuits.
**Goal applicability**: General strength (B1) · Strength peak (B2) · Strength endurance (B3) · Hybrid athlete (C4) · Team sport season prep (C9)
**Video URL**: *placeholder*
**Sources**: Fenwick, C. et al. (2009). Comparison of different rowing exercises: trunk muscle activation and lumbar spine motion, load, and stiffness. J Strength Cond Res. · Schoenfeld, B. (2010). Squatting kinematics and kinetics and their application to exercise performance. J Strength Cond Res.

entries.heading: 16. T-Bar Row
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Horizontal pull
**Primary**: Lats · Rhomboids · Mid-trapezius
**Secondary**: Biceps · Erector spinae · Posterior deltoid
**Equipment**: T-bar row machine or barbell + landmine attachment + V-handle. *Swaps*: barbell row · chest-supported row · seal row · Cluster 3 #55 Cable Row
**Unilateral**: No (single-arm landmine row variant)
**Difficulty**: Intermediate
**Tags**: compound · accessory · hypertrophy · back-dominant
**Form cues**:
Hinge at hips, slight knee bend
Grip handle, hang from arms
Pull to belly button area
Squeeze shoulder blades
Control descent
**Common errors**:
Standing too upright
Jerking weight up
Using arms-only
Partial ROM
**Substitution alternatives**: Chest-supported row · barbell row · Cluster 3 #55 Cable Row · seal row
**Pairing logic**: Pairs with horizontal push. Pairs with arm/biceps work. Less ideal stacked with deadlifts.
**Goal applicability**: Build muscle (A2) · General strength (B1) · Team sport season prep (C9) · General health maintenance (D1) · Menopause-aware training (F5) · Arm focus (G2) · Athletic look (G3)
**Video URL**: *placeholder*
**Sources**: Fenwick, C. et al. (2009). Comparison of different rowing exercises. J Strength Cond Res. · Schoenfeld, B. Science and Development of Muscle Hypertrophy (Human Kinetics, 2nd ed. 2020).

entries.heading: 17. Pull-up
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Vertical pull
**Primary**: Lats · Biceps
**Secondary**: Mid-trapezius · Rhomboids · Forearms · Core
**Equipment**: Pull-up bar. *Swaps*: assisted pull-up (band, machine, or partner) · Cluster 3 #54 Lat Pulldown · inverted row (for scaling)
**Unilateral**: No (one-arm progression is advanced calisthenics)
**Difficulty**: Intermediate–Advanced (bodyweight strength gate)
**Tags**: compound · primary movement · bodyweight · strength · hypertrophy
**Form cues**:
Hang with shoulders engaged (don't dead-hang slack)
Pull elbows down and back
Chin clears bar
Controlled descent
Full range every rep
**Common errors**:
Half-reps
Kipping unconsciously
Craning neck instead of pulling chest up
Letting shoulders shrug at top
**Substitution alternatives**: Assisted pull-up · Cluster 3 #54 Lat Pulldown · band-assisted pull-up · inverted row · negative pull-ups (for progression)
**Pairing logic**: Pairs excellently with overhead press as antagonist. Pairs with dips for upper body push-pull. Works well in supersets with horizontal push.
**Goal applicability**: Build muscle (A2) · General strength (B1) · Strength endurance (B3) · Hybrid athlete (C4) · Climbing/bouldering (C8) · Team sport season prep (C9) · General health maintenance (D1) · Menopause-aware training (F5) · Arm focus (G2) · Athletic look (G3)
**Video URL**: *placeholder*
**Sources**: Youdas, J. et al. (2010). Surface electromyographic activation patterns and elbow joint motion during a pull-up, chin-up, or perfect-pullup rotational exercise. J Strength Cond Res. · Hewit, J. et al. (2018). A comparison of muscle activation during the pull-up and three alternative pulling exercises. J Phys Fit Treatment & Sports.

entries.heading: 18. Chin-up
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Vertical pull
**Primary**: Lats · Biceps
**Secondary**: Mid-trapezius · Rhomboids · Forearms · Core
**Equipment**: Pull-up bar. *Swaps*: assisted chin-up (band/machine) · neutral grip pull-up · supinated Cluster 3 #54 Lat Pulldown
**Unilateral**: No
**Difficulty**: Intermediate (slightly easier than pull-up due to biceps leverage)
**Tags**: compound · bodyweight · strength · hypertrophy
**Form cues**:
Supinated grip, hands shoulder-width
Same hang and pull mechanics as pull-up
Chin clears bar
Controlled descent
**Common errors**:
Swinging body for momentum
Half ROM
Letting shoulders shrug
**Substitution alternatives**: Pull-up · assisted chin-up · supinated Cluster 3 #54 Lat Pulldown · band-assisted chin-up
**Pairing logic**: Pairs with horizontal pushing. Pairs with triceps work as upper-body push-pull. Pairs as biceps-dominant variant of vertical pull.
**Goal applicability**: Build muscle (A2) · General strength (B1) · Strength endurance (B3) · Hybrid athlete (C4) · Climbing/bouldering (C8) · General health maintenance (D1) · Arm focus (G2) · Athletic look (G3)
**Video URL**: *placeholder*
**Sources**: Youdas, J. et al. (2010). Surface electromyographic activation patterns and elbow joint motion during a pull-up, chin-up, or perfect-pullup rotational exercise. J Strength Cond Res. · Doma, K. et al. (2013). The reliability of chin-ups as a measure of upper body strength. J Strength Cond Res.

entries.heading: 19. Weighted Pull-up
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Vertical pull
**Primary**: Lats · Biceps
**Secondary**: Mid-trapezius · Rhomboids · Forearms · Core
**Equipment**: Pull-up bar, dip belt + plates or weighted vest. *Swaps*: weighted chin-up · Cluster 3 #54 Lat Pulldown (heavier load) · band-resisted pull-up
**Unilateral**: No
**Difficulty**: Advanced (requires bodyweight pull-up baseline)
**Tags**: compound · strength · hypertrophy · loading progression
**Form cues**:
Same form as pull-up
Attach load via dip belt or vest
Pause at chin-over-bar briefly
Controlled eccentric
Don't let weight swing
**Common errors**:
Adding weight before bodyweight form is solid
Half ROM
Momentum
Letting weight swing during descent
**Substitution alternatives**: Weighted chin-up · Cluster 3 #54 Lat Pulldown (heavier load) · pull-up at higher rep ranges
**Pairing logic**: Pairs with weighted dip as upper-body strength duo. Pairs with rowing. Poor as fatigue accumulator (form degrades).

entries.heading: 20. Farmer's Carry
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Carry (loaded locomotion)
**Primary**: Trapezius · Forearms · Core (anti-lateral flexion)
**Secondary**: Glutes · Quadriceps · Calves · Postural musculature
**Equipment**: Heavy dumbbells, kettlebells, or specialty trap-handles. *Swaps*: suitcase carry (single-side) · trap bar carry · kettlebell carry
**Unilateral**: No (suitcase carry is unilateral variant)
**Difficulty**: Beginner–Intermediate
**Tags**: compound · accessory · core · grip · conditioning
**Form cues**:
Stand tall, ribcage stacked over hips
Shoulders pulled back
Take controlled steps
Brace core throughout
Breathe under load
**Common errors**:
Shoulders rolling forward
Ribcage flaring
Short shuffling steps
Holding breath unintentionally
Loading too heavy too fast (grip fails before legs)
**Substitution alternatives**: Suitcase carry · trap bar carry · kettlebell racked carry · weighted vest walking
**Pairing logic**: Excellent finisher. Pairs with grip work. Pairs with core anti-rotation. Works in many conditioning circuits.
**Goal applicability**: Build muscle (A2) · General strength (B1) · Strength endurance (B3) · Hybrid athlete (C4) · Combat sports prep (C6) · Team sport season prep (C9) · General health maintenance (D1) · Bone density (D4) · Lower back rehab (Phase 2+) (E2) · Senior fitness (F6) · Athletic look (G3)

entries.heading: 21. Hip Thrust
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Hinge (horizontal hip extension)
**Primary**: Glutes
**Secondary**: Hamstrings · Quadriceps · Core
**Equipment**: Barbell, plates, bench, hip pad. *Swaps*: dumbbell hip thrust · single-leg hip thrust · machine hip thrust · glute bridge (floor)
**Unilateral**: No (single-leg variant exists)
**Difficulty**: Beginner–Intermediate
**Tags**: accessory · hypertrophy · glute-dominant
**Form cues**:
Upper back on bench, mid-shoulder-blade contact
Feet flat, knees ~90° at top
Drive through heels, ribs neutral
Squeeze glutes at top, brief pause
Control descent
**Common errors**:
Hyperextending lower back at top
Pushing through toes (loses glute drive)
Bar drifting up the body across the set
Insufficient ROM at top
**Substitution alternatives**: Dumbbell hip thrust · machine hip thrust · single-leg hip thrust · glute bridge · cable pull-through
**Pairing logic**: Excellent paired with quad-dominant work (squat, lunge). Pairs with RDL as posterior chain duo. Layer 1 staple in supersets.
**Goal applicability**: Get lean (A1) · Build muscle (A2) · Sustainable fat loss (A4) · General strength (B1) · Strength endurance (B3) · Hybrid athlete (C4) · Team sport season prep (C9) · General health maintenance (D1) · Bone density (D4) · Mobility & joint health (D5) · Knee rehab (E1) · Lower back rehab, Phase 2 (E2) · Hip rehab (E4) · Postpartum reconditioning, Phase 2+ (F4) · Menopause-aware training (F5) · Senior fitness (F6) · Glute development (G1) · Athletic look (G3)

entries.heading: 22. Single-Leg Hip Thrust
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Hinge (unilateral horizontal hip extension)
**Primary**: Glutes
**Secondary**: Hamstrings · Core (anti-rotation) · Quadriceps
**Equipment**: Bench, optional dumbbell on hip. *Swaps*: hip thrust (bilateral) · single-leg glute bridge · cable single-leg pull-through
**Unilateral**: Yes
**Difficulty**: Intermediate
**Tags**: accessory · unilateral · hypertrophy · stability
**Form cues**:
Same upper-back contact as bilateral hip thrust
Lift one leg off floor, drive through working heel
Keep hips level (don't drop on free side)
Squeeze glute hard at top
Control descent
**Common errors**:
Hip dropping on non-working side (rotation compensation)
Hyperextending lumbar
Pushing off the free leg
Insufficient ROM
**Substitution alternatives**: Hip thrust (bilateral) · single-leg glute bridge · cable single-leg pull-through · single-leg deadlift
**Pairing logic**: Pairs in supersets with single-leg quad work. Excellent for asymmetry correction. Less ideal as primary lift — use bilateral for heaviest stimulus.
**Goal applicability**: Get lean (A1) · General strength (B1) · Race prep, short distance (C1) · Race prep, long distance (C2) · Trail running (C3) · Racquet sports (C7) · Team sport season prep (C9) · Mobility & joint health (D5) · Knee rehab (E1) · Hip rehab (E4) · Postpartum reconditioning, Phase 2+ (F4) · Glute development (G1)

entries.heading: 23. Single-Leg RDL
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Hinge (unilateral)
**Primary**: Hamstrings · Glutes
**Secondary**: Erector spinae · Core (anti-rotation) · Calves (balance)
**Equipment**: Dumbbell or kettlebell. *Swaps*: B-stance RDL · regular RDL · cable single-leg pull-through · landmine single-leg RDL
**Unilateral**: Yes
**Difficulty**: Intermediate (balance demand)
**Tags**: accessory · unilateral · hypertrophy · stability · rehab-friendly
**Form cues**:
Soft knee, slight bend
Hinge at hip, raise opposite leg behind as counterweight
Hips stay square (don't rotate open)
Lower until hamstring stretch, weight close to leg
Drive through standing heel to return
**Common errors**:
Rotating hips open (loses unilateral demand)
Bending the supporting knee too much (becomes single-leg squat)
Rounding lower back at the bottom
Reaching weight too far forward
**Substitution alternatives**: B-stance RDL · regular RDL · cable single-leg pull-through · supported single-leg RDL
**Pairing logic**: Pairs in supersets with single-leg quad work. Excellent for hamstring asymmetry. Demanding on stability — keep moderate volume.
**Goal applicability**: Get lean (A1) · Sustainable fat loss (A4) · General strength (B1) · Strength endurance (B3) · Race prep, short distance (C1) · Race prep, long distance (C2) · Trail running (C3) · Cycling event prep (C5) · Racquet sports (C7) · Team sport season prep (C9) · General health maintenance (D1) · Mobility & joint health (D5) · Knee rehab (E1) · Hip rehab (E4) · Postpartum reconditioning, Phase 2+ (F4) · Menopause-aware training (F5) · Senior fitness (F6) · Glute development (G1)

entries.heading: 24. Good Morning
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Hinge
**Primary**: Hamstrings · Glutes · Erector spinae
**Secondary**: Adductors · Core
**Equipment**: Barbell, plates, rack. *Swaps*: cable pull-through · seated good morning · banded good morning · RDL
**Unilateral**: No
**Difficulty**: Intermediate (technique-sensitive, lower-back loaded)
**Tags**: accessory · strength · hamstring/glute · technique-sensitive
**Form cues**:
Bar on upper back, like high-bar squat
Soft knees, hinge at hips
Push hips back, chest forward
Maintain neutral spine throughout
Stand by driving hips forward
**Common errors**:
Squatting instead of hinging
Lower back rounding under load
Going too heavy too fast
Holding breath without bracing
**Substitution alternatives**: Cable pull-through · seated good morning · RDL · banded good morning
**Pairing logic**: Pairs as primary hamstring stimulus on quad-dominant days. Poor pair with heavy deadlift same session (low-back overlap).
**Goal applicability**: General strength (B1) · Strength peak (B2) · Strength endurance (B3) · Team sport season prep (C9)

entries.heading: 25. Cable Pull-Through
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Hinge
**Primary**: Glutes · Hamstrings
**Secondary**: Erector spinae · Core
**Equipment**: Cable machine, rope attachment. *Swaps*: kettlebell swing · banded pull-through · RDL · hip thrust
**Unilateral**: No (single-arm variant exists)
**Difficulty**: Beginner
**Tags**: accessory · hypertrophy · glute · low-back-friendly
**Form cues**:
Face away from cable, rope between legs
Hinge at hips, soft knees
Drive hips forward, squeeze glutes at top
Control eccentric back to start
Don't lean back at lockout
**Common errors**:
Squatting the movement
Using lower back to extend at top instead of glutes
Going too heavy (form deteriorates)
**Substitution alternatives**: Kettlebell swing · banded pull-through · RDL · hip thrust
**Pairing logic**: Pairs with quad-dominant work. Excellent low-back-friendly hinge alternative when deadlift volume is high.
**Goal applicability**: Get lean (A1) · Sustainable fat loss (A4) · General strength (B1) · Strength endurance (B3) · Hybrid athlete (C4) · General health maintenance (D1) · Mobility & joint health (D5) · Lower back rehab, Phase 2 (E2) · Hip rehab (E4) · Glute development (G1)

entries.heading: 26. Glute Bridge
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Hinge (horizontal hip extension, floor)
**Primary**: Glutes
**Secondary**: Hamstrings · Core
**Equipment**: Bodyweight or barbell, dumbbell, plate. *Swaps*: hip thrust (more ROM) · single-leg glute bridge · banded glute bridge · frog pump
**Unilateral**: No (single-leg version available)
**Difficulty**: Beginner
**Tags**: accessory · activation · hypertrophy · rehab-friendly · low-load
**Form cues**:
Lying flat, knees bent, feet flat
Drive through heels
Squeeze glutes at top, ribs down
Don't hyperextend lumbar spine
Control descent
**Common errors**:
Pushing through toes
Hyperextending lower back
Letting knees fall in or out
Not reaching full hip extension
**Substitution alternatives**: Hip thrust · single-leg glute bridge · banded glute bridge · frog pump
**Pairing logic**: Excellent activation work pre-strength. Pairs as accessory after compound hip work. Frequently used in rehab and warm-up.
**Goal applicability**: Get lean (A1) · General health maintenance (D1) · Mobility & joint health (D5) · Lower back rehab, Phase 1 (E2) · Hip rehab, Phase 1 (E4) · Postpartum reconditioning, Phase 1 (F4) · Senior fitness (F6) · Glute development (G1)

entries.heading: 27. Bulgarian Split Squat
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Squat (unilateral)
**Primary**: Quadriceps · Glutes
**Secondary**: Adductors · Hamstrings · Core (anti-rotation)
**Equipment**: Bench, dumbbells or barbell. *Swaps*: split squat (no elevation) · walking lunge · reverse lunge · step-up
**Unilateral**: Yes
**Difficulty**: Intermediate
**Tags**: compound · accessory · unilateral · hypertrophy · stability
**Form cues**:
Rear foot on bench, instep down
Front foot far enough forward (knee tracks over mid-foot)
Lower straight down, controlled
Front heel stays planted
Drive through full foot to stand
**Common errors**:
Front foot too close (knee passes far over toe)
Pushing off rear leg
Front knee caving inward
Trunk leaning excessively forward
**Substitution alternatives**: Split squat (no elevation) · walking lunge · reverse lunge · step-up · single-leg leg press
**Pairing logic**: Pairs with hinge-dominant work or upper body. Layer 1 staple in B-supersets. Excellent for asymmetry. Pairs less well after heavy back squat (quad overload).

entries.heading: 28. Walking Lunge
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Squat (unilateral, locomotion)
**Primary**: Quadriceps · Glutes
**Secondary**: Hamstrings · Adductors · Core
**Equipment**: Bodyweight, dumbbells, or barbell. Open space. *Swaps*: reverse lunge · forward lunge (in place) · BSS · step-up
**Unilateral**: Yes (alternating)
**Difficulty**: Beginner–Intermediate
**Tags**: accessory · unilateral · hypertrophy · conditioning
**Form cues**:
Step forward into stance, knee bends to ~90°
Front knee tracks over mid-foot
Drive through front heel to step into next rep
Maintain upright torso
Steady tempo, controlled
**Common errors**:
Step too short (knee shoots over toe)
Letting knee cave inward
Trunk leaning forward
Bouncing through reps
**Substitution alternatives**: Reverse lunge · BSS · forward lunge · step-up
**Pairing logic**: Pairs with hinge work. Useful as conditioning finisher. Less ideal stacked with BSS (overlapping stimulus).
**Goal applicability**: Build muscle (A2) · Sustainable fat loss (A4) · General strength (B1) · Strength endurance (B3) · Hybrid athlete (C4) · Combat sports prep (C6) · Racquet sports (C7) · Team sport season prep (C9) · General health maintenance (D1) · Menopause-aware training (F5) · Senior fitness (F6) · Glute development (G1)

entries.heading: 29. Reverse Lunge
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Squat (unilateral)
**Primary**: Quadriceps · Glutes
**Secondary**: Hamstrings · Adductors · Core
**Equipment**: Bodyweight, dumbbells, or barbell. *Swaps*: walking lunge · forward lunge · split squat · BSS
**Unilateral**: Yes
**Difficulty**: Beginner (more knee-friendly than forward lunge)
**Tags**: accessory · unilateral · hypertrophy · knee-friendly
**Form cues**:
Step backward into stance
Front foot stays planted, knee tracks over mid-foot
Back knee approaches floor with control
Drive through front heel to return to standing
Stay tall throughout
**Common errors**:
Step too short or too long
Pushing off back foot to assist
Front knee caving in
Leaning forward
**Substitution alternatives**: BSS · walking lunge · forward lunge · split squat
**Pairing logic**: Pairs as quad-dominant accessory with upper body or hip-dominant work. Often gentler on knees than forward lunge — useful in rehab.
**Goal applicability**: Sustainable fat loss (A4) · General strength (B1) · Strength endurance (B3) · Team sport season prep (C9) · General health maintenance (D1) · Mobility & joint health (D5) · Knee rehab, Phase 2 (E1) · Postpartum reconditioning, Phase 2+ (F4) · Senior fitness (F6) · Glute development (G1)

entries.heading: 30. Step-Up
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Squat (unilateral, vertical)
**Primary**: Quadriceps · Glutes
**Secondary**: Hamstrings · Calves · Core
**Equipment**: Box or bench (knee-height), optional dumbbells/barbell. *Swaps*: BSS · reverse lunge · single-leg press · split squat
**Unilateral**: Yes
**Difficulty**: Beginner–Intermediate
**Tags**: accessory · unilateral · hypertrophy · functional · rehab-friendly
**Form cues**:
Place full foot on box (not just toe)
Drive through heel of working leg
Don't push off ground with back foot
Stand fully on top, control descent
Box height: knee at ~90° at start
**Common errors**:
Pushing off the trailing leg (loses unilateral emphasis)
Box too low (insufficient stimulus)
Hopping up
Letting knee cave in
**Substitution alternatives**: BSS · reverse lunge · split squat · single-leg leg press
**Pairing logic**: Excellent rehab and beginner unilateral. Pairs with hip-dominant work or upper body. Foundational functional choice.
**Goal applicability**: Sustainable fat loss (A4) · General strength (B1) · Team sport season prep (C9) · General health maintenance (D1) · Bone density (D4) · Knee rehab, Phase 2 (E1) · Hip rehab (E4) · Postpartum reconditioning, Phase 2+ (F4) · Senior fitness (F6) · Glute development (G1)

entries.heading: 31. Goblet Squat
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Squat
**Primary**: Quadriceps · Glutes
**Secondary**: Adductors · Core · Upper back (anti-flexion)
**Equipment**: Dumbbell or kettlebell. *Swaps*: front squat · back squat · zercher squat
**Unilateral**: No
**Difficulty**: Beginner
**Tags**: compound · accessory · technique · scaling option · rehab-applicable
**Form cues**:
Hold weight at chest, elbows tucked
Sit between hips
Keep chest up, weight close to body
Drive through full foot
Stand tall
**Common errors**:
Letting elbows flare out
Forward lean (load too heavy)
Cutting depth
Heels lifting (ankle mobility limit)
**Substitution alternatives**: Front squat · back squat · zercher squat · belt squat
**Pairing logic**: Excellent for warm-up, technique work, and lighter accessory volume. Pairs with most accessories. Critical regression for Reactivator and post-rehab populations.

entries.heading: 32. Nordic Hamstring Curl
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Hinge (knee flexion eccentric)
**Primary**: Hamstrings (eccentric emphasis)
**Secondary**: Glutes · Calves · Core
**Equipment**: Anchored feet (partner, loaded barbell, GHR pad, or specialty device). *Swaps*: razor curl · GHR · stability ball leg curl · partner-assisted Nordic
**Unilateral**: No (single-leg variant available)
**Difficulty**: Advanced (eccentric strength gate)
**Tags**: accessory · hypertrophy · eccentric · injury-prevention · hamstring
**Form cues**:
Anchor feet (heels under pads or held)
Knees on padded surface
Body straight from knees up
Lower under control as far as eccentric strength allows
Catch with hands at end of ROM, push back to start
**Common errors**:
Hinging at hips (not maintaining straight body)
Falling at end of ROM uncontrolled
Going too deep too soon (injury cluster)
Using arms to push too early
**Substitution alternatives**: Razor curl · GHR · stability ball leg curl · partner-assisted Nordic
**Pairing logic**: Excellent injury-prevention tool, particularly for runners and field-sport athletes. Demanding — moderate volume (3 sets × 5–10 reps, 1–2×/week). Soreness often substantial first weeks.
**Goal applicability**: General strength (B1) · Strength endurance (B3) · Race prep, short distance (C1) · Race prep, long distance (C2) · Trail running (C3) · Team sport season prep (C9) · Youth athletics (F7) · Glute development (G1)

entries.heading: 33. Dip
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Vertical push (anterior, downward)
**Primary**: Triceps · Pectoralis (sternal head) · Anterior deltoid
**Secondary**: Core · Lats (stabilizer)
**Equipment**: Parallel bars or dip station. Optional dip belt for loading. *Swaps*: bench dip · machine assisted dip · ring dip · close-grip bench press
**Unilateral**: No
**Difficulty**: Intermediate (bodyweight strength gate)
**Tags**: compound · bodyweight · strength · hypertrophy
**Form cues**:
Start at top, arms locked
Slight forward lean for chest emphasis (more upright = triceps emphasis)
Lower until upper arm parallel to floor
Drive back to lockout
Don't let shoulders shrug at bottom
**Common errors**:
Going below 90° elbow (excess shoulder stress for many)
Excessive forward lean (becomes shoulder-dominant)
Half ROM
Kipping or swinging
**Substitution alternatives**: Bench dip · machine assisted dip · close-grip bench press · push-up
**Pairing logic**: Pairs excellently with pull-ups for upper-body push-pull. Pairs with rowing. Heavy dips poor stacked with heavy bench (overlapping pec/triceps load).
**Goal applicability**: Build muscle (A2) · General strength (B1) · Strength endurance (B3) · Hybrid athlete (C4) · Climbing/bouldering (C8) · Team sport season prep (C9) · General health maintenance (D1) · Menopause-aware training (F5) · Arm focus (G2) · Athletic look (G3)

entries.heading: 34. Dumbbell Bench Press
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Horizontal push
**Primary**: Pectoralis major · Anterior deltoid · Triceps
**Secondary**: Core (stabilization) · Lats
**Equipment**: Dumbbells, bench. *Swaps*: barbell bench press · machine chest press · push-up · floor press dumbbell
**Unilateral**: No (single-arm version exists)
**Difficulty**: Beginner–Intermediate
**Tags**: compound · accessory · hypertrophy · stabilizer-demand
**Form cues**:
Set up like barbell bench (planted feet, retracted scapulae)
Dumbbells start over chest
Lower with control, dumbbells trace slight arc
Press back to start, dumbbells nearly touching
Don't clang at top (loses stability)
**Common errors**:
Letting dumbbells drift wide (shoulder strain)
Asymmetric pressing (one side ahead)
Bouncing weights at chest
Insufficient ROM
**Substitution alternatives**: Barbell bench press · machine chest press · floor press dumbbell · push-up variations
**Pairing logic**: Pairs with rowing variants. Pairs with arm/shoulder isolation. Often used when barbell unavailable or for hypertrophy variation. Greater stretch at bottom than barbell variant.
**Goal applicability**: Build muscle (A2) · Body recomposition (A3) · Sustainable fat loss (A4) · General strength (B1) · Strength endurance (B3) · Team sport season prep (C9) · General health maintenance (D1) · Menopause-aware training (F5) · Arm focus (G2) · Athletic look (G3)

entries.heading: 35. Dumbbell Shoulder Press
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Vertical push
**Primary**: Anterior deltoid · Lateral deltoid · Triceps
**Secondary**: Core (anti-extension if standing) · Trapezius
**Equipment**: Dumbbells, bench (seated) or no bench (standing). *Swaps*: barbell overhead press · machine shoulder press · landmine press · single-arm DB press
**Unilateral**: No (single-arm version available)
**Difficulty**: Beginner–Intermediate
**Tags**: compound · accessory · hypertrophy · stabilizer-demand
**Form cues**:
Dumbbells at shoulder height, palms forward (or neutral grip)
Press straight up, dumbbells nearly touch at top
Don't lock out so hard the shoulders shrug
Brace core if standing
Control eccentric
**Common errors**:
Pressing dumbbells out wide (loses pressing stimulus)
Excessive lower-back arch (standing)
Asymmetric pressing
Letting dumbbells drift forward
**Substitution alternatives**: Barbell overhead press · machine shoulder press · landmine press · single-arm DB press
**Pairing logic**: Pairs with rowing/pulling. Pairs with arm work. Pairs less well after heavy bench (shoulder fatigue). Accessible vertical-press variant when barbell overhead is contraindicated.
**Goal applicability**: Build muscle (A2) · Sustainable fat loss (A4) · General strength (B1) · Strength endurance (B3) · General health maintenance (D1) · Menopause-aware training (F5) · Senior fitness (F6) · Arm focus (G2) · Athletic look (G3)

entries.heading: 36. Push-Up
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Horizontal push
**Primary**: Pectoralis major · Anterior deltoid · Triceps
**Secondary**: Core (full-body plank) · Serratus anterior · Glutes (stability)
**Equipment**: Bodyweight (optional weight vest or band). *Swaps*: knee push-up (scaling) · incline push-up (scaling) · decline push-up (advanced) · diamond push-up · weighted push-up
**Unilateral**: No (one-arm push-up is advanced calisthenics)
**Difficulty**: Beginner (with progressions)
**Tags**: compound · bodyweight · scaling · core
**Form cues**:
Hands slightly wider than shoulders
Body in straight line, head to heels
Brace core throughout
Lower with control, chest near floor
Drive through palms back to start
**Common errors**:
Hips sagging (loses core)
Hips piking up (loses pec stretch)
Half ROM
Elbows flared 90° (shoulder strain)
**Substitution alternatives**: Knee push-up · incline push-up · decline push-up · weighted push-up · ring push-up
**Pairing logic**: Pairs with rowing or pulling. Excellent finisher or warm-up. Used heavily in rehab progressions. Endless progression versions.
**Goal applicability**: Sustainable fat loss (A4) · Major weight loss (A5) · General strength (B1) · Strength endurance (B3) · Hybrid athlete (C4) · Combat sports prep (C6) · Team sport season prep (C9) · General health maintenance (D1) · Bone density (D4) · Lower back rehab, Phase 2 (E2) · Shoulder rehab, Phase 2 (E3) · Postpartum reconditioning, Phase 2 (F4) · Senior fitness (F6) · Youth athletics (F7) · Arm focus (G2)
**Video URL**: *placeholder*
**Sources**: Calatayud, J. et al. (2014). Bench press and push-up at comparable levels of muscle activity result in similar strength gains. J Strength Cond Res. · Cogley, R. et al. (2005). Comparison of muscle activation using various hand positions during the push-up exercise. J Strength Cond Res.

entries.heading: 37. Dumbbell Row (One-Arm)
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Horizontal pull (unilateral)
**Primary**: Lats · Rhomboids · Mid-trapezius
**Secondary**: Biceps · Posterior deltoid · Core (anti-rotation) · Erector spinae
**Equipment**: Dumbbell, bench. *Swaps*: chest-supported row · Cluster 3 #55 Cable Row · barbell row · landmine row
**Unilateral**: Yes
**Difficulty**: Beginner–Intermediate
**Tags**: compound · accessory · unilateral · hypertrophy · back-dominant
**Form cues**:
Knee and hand on bench, opposite leg planted
Pull dumbbell to hip, elbow tucked
Squeeze shoulder blade
Control descent, full stretch at bottom
Don't rotate torso
**Common errors**:
Twisting torso to lift heavier (cheats lats)
Pulling with arm only (no scapular movement)
Dumbbell drifting forward (becomes upright row)
Half ROM
**Substitution alternatives**: Chest-supported row · Cluster 3 #55 Cable Row · barbell row · landmine row · meadows row
**Pairing logic**: Layer 1 staple in Upper Push/Pull supersets. Excellent for asymmetry and core engagement. Pairs with horizontal push.
**Goal applicability**: Build muscle (A2) · Body recomposition (A3) · Sustainable fat loss (A4) · General strength (B1) · Hybrid athlete (C4) · Team sport season prep (C9) · General health maintenance (D1) · Postpartum reconditioning, Phase 2+ (F4) · Menopause-aware training (F5) · Senior fitness (F6) · Arm focus (G2) · Athletic look (G3)
**Video URL**: *placeholder*
**Sources**: Fenwick, C. et al. (2009). Comparison of different rowing exercises: trunk muscle activation and lumbar spine motion, load, and stiffness. J Strength Cond Res. · Lehman, G. et al. (2004). The importance of normalisation in the interpretation of surface electromyography. J Manipulative Physiol Ther.

entries.heading: 38. Inverted Row
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Horizontal pull (bodyweight)
**Primary**: Lats · Mid-trapezius · Rhomboids · Posterior deltoid
**Secondary**: Biceps · Core · Glutes
**Equipment**: Bar in rack at hip-to-chest height, gymnastic rings, or TRX. *Swaps*: ring row · TRX row · Cluster 3 #55 Cable Row · chest-supported row
**Unilateral**: No (single-arm progression exists)
**Difficulty**: Beginner (progresses to advanced via body angle)
**Tags**: bodyweight · accessory · scaling · pull · rehab-friendly
**Form cues**:
Body straight from head to heels (or knees if scaled)
Grip bar with arms extended
Pull chest toward bar, elbows tucked
Active scapula at bottom (don't slump)
Control descent
**Common errors**:
Hips sagging
Insufficient ROM (chest doesn't approach bar)
Using legs to push off floor
Letting head jut forward
**Substitution alternatives**: Ring row · TRX row · Cluster 3 #55 Cable Row · dumbbell row · chest-supported row
**Pairing logic**: Excellent pull-up progression. Pairs with push-ups for bodyweight upper-body work. Adjust difficulty by body angle (more horizontal = harder).
**Goal applicability**: Sustainable fat loss (A4) · Major weight loss (A5) · General strength (B1) · Hybrid athlete (C4) · Combat sports prep (C6) · Team sport season prep (C9) · General health maintenance (D1) · Bone density (D4) · Shoulder rehab, Phase 2 (E3) · Postpartum reconditioning, Phase 2 (F4) · Senior fitness (F6) · Youth athletics (F7) · Arm focus (G2)
**Video URL**: *placeholder*
**Sources**: Youdas, J. et al. (2010). Surface electromyographic activation patterns during a pull-up, chin-up, or perfect-pullup exercise. J Strength Cond Res. · Snarr, R., Esco, M. (2014). EMG comparison of the inverted row and bodyweight row. J Strength Cond Res.

entries.heading: 39. Face Pull
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Horizontal pull (high)
**Primary**: Posterior deltoid · Mid-trapezius · Rhomboids · External rotators
**Secondary**: Biceps · Forearms
**Equipment**: Cable machine, rope attachment (or band). *Swaps*: band pull-apart · prone Y-T-W · reverse fly · band face pull
**Unilateral**: No
**Difficulty**: Beginner
**Tags**: accessory · activation · postural · rehab-friendly · shoulder-health
**Form cues**:
Cable at face height, rope grip with thumbs back
Pull rope to face, separating hands at end (external rotation)
Elbows high, squeeze shoulder blades
Pause briefly at end range
Control return
**Common errors**:
Going too heavy (loses form, becomes shrug or row)
Insufficient external rotation at end
Letting elbows drop (becomes high row)
Using torso momentum
**Substitution alternatives**: Band pull-apart · prone Y-T-W · reverse fly · band face pull
**Pairing logic**: Universal addition to any pressing day. Pairs with bench press as antagonist. High-frequency tolerable (3–5×/week often).
**Goal applicability**: General strength (B1) · Strength peak (B2) · Racquet sports (C7) · Team sport season prep (C9) · General health maintenance (D1) · Shoulder rehab, Phase 1+ (E3) · Menopause-aware training (F5) · Arm focus (G2) · Athletic look (G3) · Posture/desk-worker rebalancing (G4)
**Video URL**: *placeholder*
**Sources**: Cools, A. et al. (2014). Rehabilitation of scapular dyskinesis: from the office worker to the elite overhead athlete. Br J Sports Med. · Reinold, M. et al. (2009). Current concepts in the scientific and clinical rationale behind exercises for glenohumeral and scapulothoracic musculature. J Orthop Sports Phys Ther.

entries.heading: 40. Lateral Raise
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Isolation (shoulder abduction)
**Primary**: Lateral deltoid
**Secondary**: Anterior deltoid · Trapezius · Rotator cuff
**Equipment**: Dumbbells (or cable). *Swaps*: cable lateral raise · machine lateral raise · band lateral raise · leaning DB lateral raise
**Unilateral**: No (single-arm cable variant)
**Difficulty**: Beginner
**Tags**: isolation · hypertrophy · shoulder
**Form cues**:
Slight elbow bend, maintain throughout
Lead with elbows, not hands
Raise to shoulder level
Slight forward lean engages mid-delt better
Control descent — eccentric matters
**Common errors**:
Going too heavy (becomes shrug + swing)
Leading with hands (loses lateral delt emphasis)
Insufficient ROM
Locking elbows
**Substitution alternatives**: Cable lateral raise · machine lateral raise · band lateral raise · leaning lateral raise
**Pairing logic**: High-frequency tolerable (delts recover quickly at this load). Pairs in supersets with pressing or pulling. Layer 1 staple in Upper P/P session.
**Goal applicability**: Build muscle (A2) · Body recomposition (A3) · Strength endurance (B3) · Team sport season prep (C9) · General health maintenance (D1) · Menopause-aware training (F5) · Arm focus (G2) · Athletic look (G3)
**Video URL**: *placeholder*
**Sources**: Coratella, G. et al. (2020). An electromyographic analysis of lateral raise variations and frontal raise. J Hum Kinet. · Schoenfeld, B. Science and Development of Muscle Hypertrophy (Human Kinetics, 2nd ed. 2020).

entries.heading: 41. Rear Delt Fly
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Isolation (shoulder horizontal abduction)
**Primary**: Posterior deltoid · Mid-trapezius · Rhomboids
**Secondary**: Rotator cuff
**Equipment**: Dumbbells, machine, or cables. *Swaps*: face pull · prone Y-T-W · band pull-apart · cable rear delt fly
**Unilateral**: No (single-arm cable variant)
**Difficulty**: Beginner
**Tags**: isolation · hypertrophy · postural · rear-shoulder
**Form cues**:
Hinge at hips OR seated bent forward
Slight elbow bend, maintain
Lift weights out and back, leading with elbows
Squeeze rear delts
Control descent
**Common errors**:
Going too heavy (becomes row)
Using torso momentum
Insufficient ROM
Pulling elbows too high (becomes upright row)
**Substitution alternatives**: Face pull · machine rear delt fly · cable rear delt fly · prone Y-T-W
**Pairing logic**: Pairs with chest work as posterior balance. High-frequency suitable. Universal recommendation for desk-worker rebalancing.
**Goal applicability**: General strength (B1) · Team sport season prep (C9) · General health maintenance (D1) · Shoulder rehab, Phase 1+ (E3) · Athletic look (G3) · Posture/desk-worker rebalancing (G4)
**Video URL**: *placeholder*
**Sources**: Cools, A. et al. (2014). Rehabilitation of scapular dyskinesis. Br J Sports Med. · Schory, A. et al. (2017). A systematic review of the exercises that produce optimal muscle ratios of the scapular stabilizers in normal shoulders. Int J Sports Phys Ther.

entries.heading: 42. Barbell Curl
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Isolation (elbow flexion)
**Primary**: Biceps brachii
**Secondary**: Brachialis · Brachioradialis · Forearm flexors
**Equipment**: Barbell or EZ-bar. *Swaps*: dumbbell curl · cable curl · EZ-bar curl · preacher curl
**Unilateral**: No
**Difficulty**: Beginner
**Tags**: isolation · accessory · hypertrophy · arm-focus
**Form cues**:
Stand tall, elbows by sides
Curl bar up, keeping elbows fixed
Squeeze biceps at top
Control descent — eccentric matters
Don't swing torso
**Common errors**:
Swinging body to lift weight
Elbows drifting forward (loses biceps emphasis)
Half ROM
Going too heavy (form fails, wrist strain)
**Substitution alternatives**: EZ-bar curl · dumbbell curl · cable curl · preacher curl
**Pairing logic**: Pairs with triceps work as arm-focused superset. Frequently used in arm-focused blocks. Pairs as finisher.
**Goal applicability**: Build muscle (A2) · General strength (B1) · Arm focus (G2) · Athletic look (G3)
**Video URL**: *placeholder*
**Sources**: Marcolin, G. et al. (2018). Differences in electromyographic activity between dumbbell biceps curl variations. PeerJ. · Coratella, G. et al. (2023). Biceps brachii architectural responses to incline vs. preacher curl training. J Sports Sci.

entries.heading: 43. Dumbbell Curl
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Isolation (elbow flexion)
**Primary**: Biceps brachii
**Secondary**: Brachialis · Brachioradialis · Forearms
**Equipment**: Dumbbells. *Swaps*: barbell curl · cable curl · incline DB curl · concentration curl
**Unilateral**: Can be done unilateral or alternating
**Difficulty**: Beginner
**Tags**: isolation · accessory · hypertrophy · arm-focus
**Form cues**:
Standing or seated, dumbbells at sides
Curl up, supinating wrist as you go (palm faces shoulder at top)
Elbows stay fixed at sides
Squeeze, control descent
Full stretch at bottom
**Common errors**:
Swinging torso
Elbows drifting forward
Not supinating (loses long-head emphasis)
Half ROM
**Substitution alternatives**: Barbell curl · cable curl · incline DB curl · concentration curl
**Pairing logic**: Pairs with triceps as arm superset. Pairs as finisher. Variants (incline, concentration) target different biceps regions.
**Goal applicability**: Build muscle (A2) · General strength (B1) · Arm focus (G2) · Athletic look (G3)
**Video URL**: *placeholder*
**Sources**: Coratella, G. et al. (2023). Biceps brachii architectural responses to incline vs. preacher curl training. J Sports Sci. · Oliveira, L. et al. (2009). Effect of preacher curl seat angle on biceps brachii muscle activity. J Strength Cond Res.

entries.heading: 44. Hammer Curl
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Isolation (elbow flexion, neutral grip)
**Primary**: Brachialis · Brachioradialis
**Secondary**: Biceps brachii (long head) · Forearms
**Equipment**: Dumbbells. *Swaps*: rope cable curl · cross-body hammer · neutral-grip curl machine
**Unilateral**: Can be done unilateral or alternating
**Difficulty**: Beginner
**Tags**: isolation · accessory · hypertrophy · forearm-focused · brachialis
**Form cues**:
Neutral grip throughout (palms facing each other)
Curl up keeping wrists neutral
Elbows fixed at sides
Squeeze briefly at top
Control descent
**Common errors**:
Letting wrists rotate (becomes regular curl)
Swinging torso
Half ROM
**Substitution alternatives**: Rope cable curl · cross-body hammer · neutral-grip curl machine
**Pairing logic**: Pairs with biceps curls in arm sessions. Often paired with regular curls for full-arm coverage. Excellent for forearm and brachialis development that supinated curls underdose.
**Goal applicability**: General strength (B1) · Climbing/bouldering (C8) · Arm focus (G2)
**Video URL**: *placeholder*
**Sources**: Marcolin, G. et al. (2018). Differences in electromyographic activity between dumbbell biceps curl variations. PeerJ. · Coratella, G. et al. (2023). Biceps brachii architectural responses. J Sports Sci.

entries.heading: 45. Tricep Pushdown
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Isolation (elbow extension)
**Primary**: Triceps brachii (lateral and medial heads)
**Secondary**: Forearms
**Equipment**: Cable machine, straight bar or rope or V-bar. *Swaps*: dumbbell kickback · band pushdown · diamond push-up · close-grip bench press
**Unilateral**: Can be done unilateral
**Difficulty**: Beginner
**Tags**: isolation · accessory · hypertrophy · arm-focus
**Form cues**:
Stand close to cable, slight forward lean
Elbows pinned to sides
Push handle down, full lockout
Squeeze triceps at bottom
Control return, full stretch at top (handle near chest)
**Common errors**:
Elbows drifting forward (loses triceps)
Using torso to push down (becomes a row pattern)
Half ROM
Going too heavy (cheating)
**Substitution alternatives**: Dumbbell kickback · band pushdown · diamond push-up · close-grip bench press
**Pairing logic**: Pairs with biceps curls. Frequently used as finisher. Pairs in arm-focused supersets.
**Goal applicability**: Build muscle (A2) · General strength (B1) · Arm focus (G2) · Athletic look (G3)
**Video URL**: *placeholder*
**Sources**: Maeo, S. et al. (2023). Triceps brachii hypertrophy is substantially greater after elbow extension training performed in the overhead vs. neutral arm position. Eur J Sport Sci. · Boeckh-Behrens, W., Buskies, W. Fitness-Krafttraining (Rowohlt, 2002).

entries.heading: 46. Overhead Tricep Extension
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Isolation (elbow extension, overhead)
**Primary**: Triceps brachii (long head emphasized)
**Secondary**: Forearms · Core (anti-extension)
**Equipment**: Dumbbell, EZ-bar, or cable + rope. *Swaps*: skull crusher · cable overhead extension · single-arm DB overhead extension
**Unilateral**: Can be done unilateral or bilateral
**Difficulty**: Beginner–Intermediate
**Tags**: isolation · accessory · hypertrophy · long-head-emphasis
**Form cues**:
Weight starts overhead, arms locked
Lower behind head with control
Elbows stay close (don't flare wide)
Extend back to lockout
Brace core, don't arch lower back
**Common errors**:
Elbows flaring wide
Arching lower back
Half ROM
Going too heavy for stretch position
**Substitution alternatives**: Skull crusher · cable overhead extension · single-arm DB overhead extension
**Pairing logic**: Pairs with biceps work. Frequently used after pressing. Long-head stretch makes this important for full triceps development per Maeo (2023).
**Goal applicability**: Build muscle (A2) · General strength (B1) · Strength endurance (B3) · Arm focus (G2) · Athletic look (G3)
**Video URL**: *placeholder*
**Sources**: Maeo, S. et al. (2023). Triceps brachii hypertrophy is substantially greater after elbow extension training performed in the overhead vs. neutral arm position. Eur J Sport Sci. · Kassiano, W. et al. (2022). Does varying resistance exercises promote superior muscle hypertrophy and strength gains? J Strength Cond Res.

entries.heading: 47. Skull Crusher
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Isolation (elbow extension, supine)
**Primary**: Triceps brachii (all three heads)
**Secondary**: Forearms · Core (stabilizer)
**Equipment**: EZ-bar or dumbbells, bench. *Swaps*: overhead tricep extension · cable overhead extension · close-grip bench press · diamond push-up
**Unilateral**: No (DB version can be unilateral)
**Difficulty**: Intermediate (technique-sensitive)
**Tags**: isolation · accessory · hypertrophy
**Form cues**:
Lying on bench, arms vertical at start
Lower bar/dumbbells toward forehead by bending elbows
Elbows stay pointing up, shoulders fixed
Extend back to start
Don't lock elbows so hard at top
**Common errors**:
Letting elbows flare out
Elbows shifting toward face (loses triceps)
Going too heavy (form deteriorates)
Arching lower back
**Substitution alternatives**: Overhead tricep extension · cable overhead extension · close-grip bench press
**Pairing logic**: Pairs with biceps in arm sessions. Pairs as finisher after pressing. Often paired with overhead extension for full triceps coverage.
**Goal applicability**: Build muscle (A2) · General strength (B1) · Arm focus (G2) · Athletic look (G3)
**Video URL**: *placeholder*
**Sources**: Maeo, S. et al. (2023). Triceps brachii hypertrophy. Eur J Sport Sci. · Boehler, B. (2011). EMG analysis of the triceps brachii muscle during a variety of elbow extension exercises. UW-La Crosse Journal of Undergraduate Research.

entries.heading: 48. Plank
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Core (anti-extension isometric)
**Primary**: Rectus abdominis · Transverse abdominis · Obliques
**Secondary**: Glutes · Quadriceps · Shoulders (stability)
**Equipment**: Bodyweight (or weighted vest for progression). *Swaps*: forearm plank · high plank · hard-style plank · long-lever plank
**Unilateral**: No (side plank is the unilateral variant)
**Difficulty**: Beginner (with progressions)
**Tags**: core · isometric · rehab-friendly · activation
**Form cues**:
Forearms on floor, elbows under shoulders
Body in straight line: head, hips, ankles
Squeeze glutes, brace abs
Posterior pelvic tilt slightly (don't sag)
Breathe steady
**Common errors**:
Hips sagging
Hips piking up
Holding breath
Going too long (form deteriorates after ~60s for most)
**Substitution alternatives**: Hard-style plank (45-second max effort) · long-lever plank · high plank · weighted plank
**Pairing logic**: Excellent in core circuits and warm-ups. Per McGill, ~60 seconds is the upper limit before form fades; quality > duration. Frequent in rehab and prehab contexts.
**Goal applicability**: General health maintenance (D1) · Lower back rehab, Phase 1+ (E2) · Postpartum reconditioning, Phase 2+ (F4) · Senior fitness (F6) · Athletic look (G3) · Posture/desk-worker rebalancing (G4)
**Video URL**: *placeholder*
**Sources**: McGill, S. Low Back Disorders: Evidence-Based Prevention and Rehabilitation (3rd ed., Human Kinetics, 2015). · Schoenfeld, B. et al. (2014). An electromyographic comparison of a modified version of the plank with a long lever and posterior tilt versus the traditional plank exercise. Sports Biomech.

entries.heading: 49. Side Plank
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Core (anti-lateral-flexion isometric)
**Primary**: Obliques · Quadratus lumborum · Glute medius
**Secondary**: Shoulders (stability) · Adductors
**Equipment**: Bodyweight. *Swaps*: side plank with hip dip · short-lever side plank (knees) · Copenhagen plank
**Unilateral**: Yes
**Difficulty**: Beginner–Intermediate
**Tags**: core · unilateral · isometric · rehab-friendly · McGill big-3
**Form cues**:
Forearm on floor, elbow under shoulder
Body in straight line, hips lifted
Top hand on hip or extended overhead
Hold steady, breathe
McGill recommends ~10-second reps × multiple sets vs single long hold for endurance development
**Common errors**:
Hips dropping
Body tilting forward or back
Holding breath
Going too long
**Substitution alternatives**: Short-lever side plank (knees) · Copenhagen plank · cable anti-rotation work · suitcase carry
**Pairing logic**: Layer 1 staple. Pairs with anti-rotation core work. Critical for lower-back rehab (E2) per McGill.
**Goal applicability**: Build muscle (A2) · General strength (B1) · Racquet sports (C7) · Hybrid athlete (C4) · General health maintenance (D1) · Mobility & joint health (D5) · Lower back rehab (E2) · Hip rehab (E4) · Postpartum reconditioning, Phase 2+ (F4) · Senior fitness (F6) · Athletic look (G3) · Posture/desk-worker rebalancing (G4)
**Video URL**: *placeholder*
**Sources**: McGill, S. Low Back Disorders: Evidence-Based Prevention and Rehabilitation (3rd ed., Human Kinetics, 2015). · McGill, S. et al. (2010). Endurance times for low back stabilization exercises. Arch Phys Med Rehabil.

entries.heading: 50. Pallof Press
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Core (anti-rotation isometric)
**Primary**: Obliques · Transverse abdominis · Rectus abdominis
**Secondary**: Shoulders (stability) · Glutes
**Equipment**: Cable machine (or band). *Swaps*: band Pallof press · half-kneeling Pallof · standing Pallof · suitcase carry
**Unilateral**: Yes (load comes from one side)
**Difficulty**: Beginner
**Tags**: core · anti-rotation · activation · rehab-friendly
**Form cues**:
Stand perpendicular to cable
Hold handle at chest with both hands
Press straight out, resisting rotation
Hold momentarily, return with control
Brace core throughout
**Common errors**:
Letting torso rotate (defeats purpose)
Going too heavy (loses anti-rotation quality)
Holding breath
Standing too close (cable doesn't pull)
**Substitution alternatives**: Band Pallof press · half-kneeling Pallof · suitcase carry · cable wood chop (rotational version)
**Pairing logic**: Excellent in any core circuit. Pairs in supersets with bilateral lifts. Frequent rehab choice.
**Goal applicability**: Build muscle (A2) · General strength (B1) · Hybrid athlete (C4) · Racquet sports (C7) · Team sport season prep (C9) · General health maintenance (D1) · Mobility & joint health (D5) · Lower back rehab (E2) · Hip rehab (E4) · Postpartum reconditioning, Phase 2+ (F4) · Senior fitness (F6) · Arm focus (G2) · Athletic look (G3) · Posture/desk-worker rebalancing (G4)
**Video URL**: *placeholder*
**Sources**: McGill, S. Low Back Disorders: Evidence-Based Prevention and Rehabilitation (3rd ed., Human Kinetics, 2015). · Behm, D. et al. (2010). The use of instability to train the core musculature. Appl Physiol Nutr Metab.

entries.heading: 51. Hanging Leg Raise
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Core (hip flexion + spinal flexion)
**Primary**: Rectus abdominis · Hip flexors
**Secondary**: Obliques · Forearms (grip) · Lats (stabilizer)
**Equipment**: Pull-up bar. *Swaps*: hanging knee raise (easier) · captain's chair leg raise · lying leg raise · ab wheel rollout
**Unilateral**: No (alternating-leg variant exists)
**Difficulty**: Intermediate–Advanced
**Tags**: core · bodyweight · hypertrophy · grip-demanding · skill-adjacent
**Form cues**:
Hang from bar, shoulders engaged
Brace core, posteriorly tilt pelvis at start
Raise legs to ~90° (or higher with progression)
Control descent — eccentric matters
Avoid swinging
**Common errors**:
Swinging body for momentum
Insufficient ROM
Hip flexors dominant (no PPT, no abs)
Letting back hyperextend at bottom
**Substitution alternatives**: Hanging knee raise · captain's chair leg raise · lying leg raise · ab roll-out
**Pairing logic**: Layer 1 staple in core supersets. Pairs in Upper sessions. Demanding grip — sometimes precedes pull-up volume rather than follows.
**Goal applicability**: Build muscle (A2) · Body recomposition (A3) · General strength (B1) · Strength endurance (B3) · Hybrid athlete (C4) · Climbing/bouldering (C8) · General health maintenance (D1) · Menopause-aware training (F5) · Senior fitness (F6) · Arm focus (G2) · Athletic look (G3)
**Video URL**: *placeholder*
**Sources**: Escamilla, R. et al. (2010). Electromyographic analysis of traditional and nontraditional abdominal exercises. Phys Ther. · Vera-Garcia, F. et al. (2014). Core stability and the related strength tests in athletes. Strength Cond J.

entries.heading: 52. Ab Roll-Out
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Core (anti-extension)
**Primary**: Rectus abdominis · Obliques
**Secondary**: Lats · Shoulders · Hip flexors
**Equipment**: Ab wheel or barbell with plates. *Swaps*: stability ball roll-out · banded roll-out · plank · TRX fallout
**Unilateral**: No
**Difficulty**: Intermediate–Advanced
**Tags**: core · accessory · anti-extension
**Form cues**:
Start kneeling, hands on wheel
Roll out slowly, body extending
Maintain neutral spine throughout
Pull back to start using core (not arms)
Don't let lower back arch
**Common errors**:
Lower back sagging at extension
Going too far before capacity allows
Pulling back with arms (skips core)
Holding breath
**Substitution alternatives**: Stability ball roll-out · banded roll-out · TRX fallout · plank
**Pairing logic**: Pairs with most strength work. Excellent end-of-session core. Pairs poorly with heavy deadlift same session (low-back fatigue overlap).
**Goal applicability**: Build muscle (A2) · General strength (B1) · Strength endurance (B3) · Hybrid athlete (C4) · General health maintenance (D1) · Mobility & joint health (D5) · Menopause-aware training (F5) · Arm focus (G2) · Athletic look (G3)
**Video URL**: *placeholder*
**Sources**: Escamilla, R. et al. (2006). Electromyographic analysis of traditional and nontraditional abdominal exercises. Phys Ther. · McGill, S. Low Back Disorders: Evidence-Based Prevention and Rehabilitation (3rd ed., Human Kinetics, 2015).

entries.heading: 53. Dead Bug
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Core (anti-extension, contralateral coordination)
**Primary**: Rectus abdominis · Transverse abdominis
**Secondary**: Hip flexors · Shoulders
**Equipment**: Bodyweight (mat). *Swaps*: dead bug with band · dead bug with weight · bird-dog · supine 90/90 hold
**Unilateral**: Yes (alternating)
**Difficulty**: Beginner
**Tags**: core · activation · rehab-friendly · coordination
**Form cues**:
Lying on back, arms up, knees at 90°
Lower opposite arm and leg slowly
Lower back stays pressed to floor
Return, alternate sides
Brace core throughout
**Common errors**:
Lower back arching off floor
Holding breath
Going too fast
Dropping arm/leg too far
**Substitution alternatives**: Dead bug with band · bird-dog · supine 90/90 hold · curl-up
**Pairing logic**: Excellent warm-up or rehab piece. Pairs with most activation work. Frequently used in postpartum and low-back rehab.
**Goal applicability**: General strength (B1) · General health maintenance (D1) · Mobility & joint health (D5) · Lower back rehab, Phase 1 (E2) · Pregnancy mid (F2) · Postpartum reconditioning, Phase 1 (F4) · Senior fitness (F6) · Posture/desk-worker rebalancing (G4)
**Video URL**: *placeholder*
