sections.heading: Cluster 2 — Cross-reference to Cluster 3
sections.content_markdown:
The following machine-class movements are catalogued in Cluster 3 (Machines) rather than Cluster 2 (Common Accessories) because their primary distinguishing feature is the machine-based force application:
- Lat Pulldown → Cluster 3 #54
- Cable Row (Seated) → Cluster 3 #55
External references using Cluster 2 numbering should redirect to the listed Cluster 3 positions.

sections.heading: Cluster 3 — Machines
sections.content_markdown: Machines complement free-weight Cluster 1 + 2 entries by providing fixed movement paths, lower skill floors, and (often) reduced spinal or stabilizer demand. They are first-class entries — not improvised substitutions — for A1 Reactivator, A6 Postpartum, A8 Senior, and rehab-phase users for whom the free-weight version is contraindicated or premature. Each entry names which Cluster 1/2 entry it substitutes for (and which substitutes for it when the machine is unavailable).

entries.heading: 54. Lat Pulldown
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Vertical pull
**Primary**: Lats · Biceps
**Secondary**: Mid-trapezius · Rhomboids · Posterior deltoid · Forearms
**Equipment**: Cable machine with lat pulldown attachment (typically wide bar, sometimes V-handle or neutral-grip bar). *Swaps*: assisted pull-up · band-assisted pull-up · machine-assisted pull-up · inverted row (for very deconditioned users)
**Unilateral**: No (single-arm cable variant exists)
**Difficulty**: Beginner
**Tags**: machine · accessory · hypertrophy · scaling · rehab-applicable
**Form cues**:
- Sit tall, thighs locked under pads
- Grip slightly wider than shoulders (or per protocol)
- Pull elbows down and back, bar to upper chest
- Squeeze shoulder blades briefly at bottom
- Control return, full stretch at top without losing shoulder engagement
**Common errors**:
- Leaning back excessively to use bodyweight as counterweight (bar pulls to belly, not chest)
- Pulling with arms only — no scapular movement
- Bar to back of neck (shoulder strain, no extra benefit)
- Half ROM at top (arms not fully extended)
- Yanking down with momentum
**Substitution alternatives** *(ordered by similarity)*: Assisted pull-up · band-assisted pull-up · machine-assisted pull-up · Cluster 1 #17 Pull-up (when capacity allows) · inverted row #38
**Pairing logic**: Pairs with horizontal push (bench, DB bench, push-up). Pairs with arm work in supersets. Primary scaling option when pull-up capacity is below 5 clean reps. Lower skill floor than free-weight vertical pulls — accessible from session 1 for Reactivators and seniors.

entries.heading: 55. Cable Row (Seated)
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Horizontal pull
**Primary**: Lats · Rhomboids · Mid-trapezius · Posterior deltoid
**Secondary**: Biceps · Forearms · Erector spinae (light stabilization)
**Equipment**: Cable row machine with foot platform, V-handle or wide bar attachment. *Swaps*: chest-supported row · dumbbell row · machine row · TRX row
**Unilateral**: No (single-arm cable row variant)
**Difficulty**: Beginner
**Tags**: machine · accessory · hypertrophy · low-spinal-load · rehab-applicable
**Form cues**:
- Sit tall, feet planted on platform, slight knee bend
- Maintain neutral spine — no excessive forward lean at start
- Pull handle to lower ribs, elbows tucked
- Squeeze shoulder blades, brief pause
- Control return, full reach forward without losing core engagement
**Common errors**:
- Rocking torso back and forth for momentum (becomes a deadlift-row hybrid)
- Pulling handle to belly button instead of lower ribs
- Letting shoulders shrug toward ears
- Lower-back rounding on the eccentric return
- Insufficient ROM (short pull, half stretch)
**Substitution alternatives** *(ordered by similarity)*: Chest-supported row · Cluster 2 #37 DB Row One-Arm · Cluster 2 #38 Inverted Row · machine row · seated band row
**Pairing logic**: Pairs with horizontal push (bench press, push-up, chest press machine). Pairs with vertical pull in upper-body sessions. Critical option for E2 Lower back rehab Phase 2 — provides horizontal pull stimulus without the spinal loading of bent-over barbell row.
**Goal applicability**: Build muscle (A2) · Body recomposition (A3) · Sustainable fat loss (A4) · Major weight loss (A5) · General strength (B1) · Strength endurance (B3) · Hybrid athlete (C4) · Combat sports prep (C6) · Team sport season prep (C9) · General health maintenance (D1) · Lower back rehab, Phase 2+ (E2) · Shoulder rehab, Phase 2+ (E3) · Return-to-training after extended pause (E7) · Postpartum reconditioning, Phase 2+ (F4) · Menopause-aware training (F5) · Senior fitness (F6) · Arm focus (G2) · Athletic look (G3) · Posture/desk-worker rebalancing (G4)

entries.heading: 56. Leg Press
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Squat (machine, no spinal compression)
**Primary**: Quadriceps · Glutes
**Secondary**: Hamstrings · Adductors · Calves
**Equipment**: 45° leg press or horizontal leg press machine. *Swaps*: hack squat · belt squat · goblet squat · Bulgarian split squat (unilateral substitute)
**Unilateral**: No (single-leg leg press variant on most machines)
**Difficulty**: Beginner
**Tags**: machine · compound · hypertrophy · no-spinal-load · rehab-applicable · scaling
**Form cues**:
- Feet shoulder-width, mid-platform — adjust placement per knee tracking
- Lower under control, knees track over toes
- Stop before lower back rounds off the pad (hip mobility limit, not depth target)
- Drive through full foot, do not lock knees explosively at top
- Maintain glute and hip contact with pad throughout
**Common errors**:
- Shortened ROM (short presses, only knee-extension portion)
- Feet too low on platform (excess knee shear)
- Lower back rounding at depth (lifts off pad — common in users chasing depth they don't have)
- Locking knees hard at top
- Loading too heavy too fast (machine forgives form, but loads add up)
**Substitution alternatives** *(ordered by similarity)*: Hack squat (Cluster 3 #57) · belt squat · Cluster 2 #31 Goblet Squat (scaled) · Cluster 2 #27 Bulgarian Split Squat (unilateral alternative) · Cluster 1 #1 Back Squat (when free-weight is appropriate)
**Pairing logic**: Pairs with hamstring-dominant work (RDL, leg curl). Pairs with upper-body in Lower Anterior sessions. Primary compound-squat option for users with low-back contraindications, ankle/hip mobility limits, or post-rehab requiring controlled loading. NOT a replacement for back squat in trained-user strength programs — different stimulus profile (less core, less stabilizer, more pure quad/glute loading).
**Goal applicability**: Build muscle (A2) · Sustainable fat loss (A4) · Major weight loss (A5) · General strength (B1) · Strength endurance (B3) · Team sport season prep (C9) · General health maintenance (D1) · Bone density (D4) · Knee rehab, Phase 1+ (E1) · Lower back rehab, Phase 2+ (E2) · Hip rehab, Phase 2+ (E4) · Return-to-training after extended pause (E7) · Postpartum reconditioning, Phase 2+ (F4) · Menopause-aware training (F5) · Senior fitness (F6) · Youth athletics (F7) · Athletic look (G3)

A comparison of tibiofemoral joint forces and electromyographic activity during open and closed kinetic chain exercises. Am J Sports Med — leg press context for knee rehab. · da Silva, E. et al. (2008). Analysis of muscle activation during different leg press exercises at submaximum effort levels. J Strength Cond Res.

entries.heading: 57. Hack Squat
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Squat (machine, axial loading on shoulders, no spinal compression of free squat)
**Primary**: Quadriceps · Glutes
**Secondary**: Hamstrings · Adductors · Core (light stabilization)
**Equipment**: Hack squat machine (sled-loaded with shoulder pads). *Swaps*: leg press · belt squat · safety bar squat · goblet squat
**Unilateral**: No (single-leg hack squat variant on some machines)
**Difficulty**: Beginner–Intermediate
**Tags**: machine · compound · hypertrophy · axial-load · spine-friendlier · quad-dominant
**Form cues**:
- Back flat against pad, shoulders under shoulder pads
- Feet mid-platform, slightly narrower than back squat stance
- Lower under control, knees track over toes
- Hit depth (thighs parallel or below if mobility allows)
- Drive through full foot, do not lock knees hard
**Common errors**:
- Heels lifting at depth (foot placement too low on platform)
- Lower back rounding off pad at depth
- Letting knees collapse inward
- Bouncing out of the bottom
- Cutting depth (machine makes it easy to half-rep)
**Substitution alternatives** *(ordered by similarity)*: Leg press (Cluster 3 #56) · belt squat · safety bar squat · Cluster 1 #2 Front Squat · Cluster 2 #31 Goblet Squat
**Pairing logic**: Pairs with hamstring-dominant work. Pairs with upper-body or core in Lower Anterior sessions. Distinct stimulus from leg press: axial-loaded (challenges core stability and posterior chain support) but spine-friendlier than back squat (no bar on spine). Good progression bridge between leg press (lowest spinal load) and free-weight back squat. Useful for A8 Senior and A1 Reactivator with low-back history.
**Goal applicability**: Build muscle (A2) · Sustainable fat loss (A4) · General strength (B1) · Strength endurance (B3) · Team sport season prep (C9) · General health maintenance (D1) · Bone density (D4) · Knee rehab, Phase 3 (E1) · Lower back rehab, Phase 3 (E2) · Return-to-training after extended pause (E7) · Menopause-aware training (F5) · Senior fitness (F6) · Athletic look (G3)
**Video URL**: *placeholder*
**Sources**: Coratella, G. et al. (2018). The electromyographic activities of trunk and lower limb muscles during flywheel-determined leg curl exercises (sled-loaded context). J Strength Cond Res. · Schoenfeld, B. (2010). Squatting kinematics and kinetics and their application to exercise performance. J Strength Cond Res. · Loturco, I. et al. (2018). Vertically and horizontally directed muscle power exercises: relationships with top-level sprint performance — sled-pattern force production context.

entries.heading: 58. Quad Isolation (Leg Extension)
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Isolation (knee extension)
**Primary**: Quadriceps (all four heads, rectus femoris especially)
**Secondary**: (none — true isolation)
**Equipment**: Leg extension machine. *Swaps*: cable knee extension · band knee extension · sissy squat (advanced bodyweight alternative)
**Unilateral**: No (single-leg variant on most machines)
**Difficulty**: Beginner
**Tags**: machine · isolation · hypertrophy · rehab-applicable · low-skill-floor
**Form cues**:
- Sit fully back, lower-back pressed to pad
- Pad sits across ankles, not shins
- Extend knees fully (controlled lockout) — do not snap
- Brief pause at top
- Control descent — eccentric is where most of the stimulus lives
**Common errors**:
- Swinging weight up with momentum (loses quad emphasis)
- Half ROM (partial extension)
- Locking knees hard with bounce at top
- Letting hips lift off the seat
- Going too heavy too fast (knee discomfort common with aggressive loading)
**Substitution alternatives** *(ordered by similarity)*: Cable knee extension · band knee extension · sissy squat · Cluster 2 #27 Bulgarian Split Squat (compound alternative, different stimulus)
**Pairing logic**: Pairs with hamstring isolation (#59 Seated Leg Curl or #60 Lying Leg Curl) as antagonist superset — Layer 1 Lower Anterior Superset C staple. Pairs with core work. Foundational rehab exercise for E1 Knee Phase 1 — bilateral, low-load, controlled ROM is the prescribed entry point per APTA Clinical Practice Guideline for ACL rehab. Caveat: avoid heavy loads at long muscle length in users with active patellar tendinopathy mid-phase; use isometric holds instead until tendinopathy phase advances.
**Goal applicability**: Build muscle (A2) · General strength (B1) · Strength endurance (B3) · Team sport season prep (C9) · Knee rehab, Phase 1+ (E1) · Return-to-training after extended pause (E7) · Menopause-aware training (F5) · Senior fitness (F6) · Athletic look (G3)
**Video URL**: *placeholder*
**Sources**: Adams, D. et al. (2018). Knee Stability and Movement Coordination Impairments: Knee Ligament Sprain — APTA Clinical Practice Guideline (leg extension protocol for ACL rehab). J Orthop Sports Phys Ther. · Maeo, S. et al. (2021). Quadriceps muscle hypertrophy is greater after partial-range vs full-range knee extension training. Eur J Sport Sci. · Stensdotter, A. et al. (2003). Quadriceps activation in closed and in open kinetic chain exercise. Med Sci Sports Exerc.

entries.heading: 59. Seated Leg Curl
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Isolation (knee flexion, hip in flexion)
**Primary**: Hamstrings (biceps femoris, semitendinosus, semimembranosus — long-head bias due to hip-flexion position)
**Secondary**: Calves (light)
**Equipment**: Seated leg curl machine with hip pad and ankle roller. *Swaps*: lying leg curl (Cluster 3 #60) · standing single-leg curl · stability ball leg curl
**Unilateral**: No (single-leg variant on most machines)
**Difficulty**: Beginner
**Tags**: machine · isolation · hypertrophy · long-muscle-length · rehab-applicable · low-skill-floor
**Form cues**:
- Sit fully back, hip pad locked over thighs
- Roller on Achilles, not calf
- Curl heels under hard, full ROM
- Pause briefly at peak contraction
- Control eccentric — the stretch position is where the hypertrophy stimulus is strongest (long-muscle-length training rationale, Maeo 2021 / Kassiano 2023)
**Common errors**:
- Swinging weight with momentum
- Half ROM (partial curl)
- Letting hip pad lift (hips coming up)
- Excessive load that prevents full ROM
- Allowing knees to wing outward at the bottom of the eccentric
**Substitution alternatives** *(ordered by similarity)*: Lying leg curl (Cluster 3 #60 — equivalent stimulus, slightly less stretch on biceps femoris per Maeo 2021) · standing single-leg curl · stability ball leg curl · Cluster 2 #32 Nordic Hamstring Curl (eccentric-emphasis alternative) · Cluster 1 #7 RDL (compound alternative, different stimulus profile)
**Pairing logic**: Pairs with quad isolation (#58 Leg Extension) as antagonist superset — Layer 1 Lower Posterior or Lower Anterior Superset C staple. Pairs with core work. Canonical hamstring isolation choice for hypertrophy goals (A2, G1, G3): the seated position lengthens the hamstring at the knee-flexion stretch, producing greater hypertrophy response than the lying variant per current evidence. For rehab use-cases (E1 Knee Phase 1), seated and lying are functionally interchangeable; use whichever is available.
**Goal applicability**: Build muscle (A2) · General strength (B1) · Strength endurance (B3) · Team sport season prep (C9) · General health maintenance (D1) · Knee rehab, Phase 1+ (E1) · Return-to-training after extended pause (E7) · Menopause-aware training (F5) · Senior fitness (F6) · Glute development (G1) · Athletic look (G3)

(2023). Influence of muscle length on hamstring hypertrophy responses to resistance training. Sports Med. · Schoenfeld, B. Science and Development of Muscle Hypertrophy (Human Kinetics, 2nd ed. 2020).

entries.heading: 60. Lying Leg Curl
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Isolation (knee flexion, hip in neutral/extension)
**Primary**: Hamstrings (biceps femoris, semitendinosus, semimembranosus — distributed activation, less long-head bias than seated)
**Secondary**: Calves (light) · Glutes (very light hip extension support)
**Equipment**: Lying leg curl machine (prone bench with ankle roller). *Swaps*: seated leg curl (Cluster 3 #59) · standing single-leg curl · stability ball leg curl
**Unilateral**: No (single-leg variant on most machines)
**Difficulty**: Beginner
**Tags**: machine · isolation · hypertrophy · rehab-applicable · low-skill-floor · widely-available
**Form cues**:
- Lie prone, ankle roller above heel
- Hips pressed into bench (do not let hips lift during curl)
- Curl heels toward glutes, full ROM
- Pause briefly at peak contraction
- Control eccentric back to extended position
**Common errors**:
- Hips lifting off bench (uses hip extension to assist — loses hamstring emphasis)
- Swinging weight with momentum
- Half ROM (partial curl)
- Excessive load that prevents full ROM
- Roller positioned over calf instead of above heel
**Substitution alternatives** *(ordered by similarity)*: Seated leg curl (Cluster 3 #59 — preferred for hypertrophy per Maeo 2021) · standing single-leg curl · stability ball leg curl · Cluster 2 #32 Nordic Hamstring Curl · Cluster 1 #7 RDL
**Pairing logic**: Pairs with quad isolation (#58 Leg Extension) as antagonist superset. Pairs with core work. More widely available in commercial gyms than seated variant — when the user has access only to a lying leg curl, this is the default. For rehab use-cases (E1 Knee Phase 1), seated and lying are functionally interchangeable. For pure hypertrophy goals, the seated variant is preferred where available.

entries.heading: 61. Chest Press Machine
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Horizontal push (machine, fixed plane)
**Primary**: Pectoralis major · Anterior deltoid · Triceps
**Secondary**: (minimal — machine removes stabilizer demand)
**Equipment**: Chest press machine (plate-loaded or selectorized; converging-arm or fixed-grip variants). *Swaps*: Cluster 1 #9 Bench Press · Cluster 2 #34 DB Bench Press · Cluster 2 #36 Push-Up · floor press
**Unilateral**: No (most machines allow single-arm, but most users default to bilateral)
**Difficulty**: Beginner
**Tags**: machine · compound · hypertrophy · low-skill-floor · rehab-applicable · no-spotter-needed
**Form cues**:
- Adjust seat so handles align with mid-chest at start
- Sit tall, scapulae retracted against pad
- Press to full but not aggressive lockout
- Control return, full stretch without losing scapular position
- Feet planted, do not push through legs for momentum
**Common errors**:
- Seat too high or too low (handles align wrong, shoulder strain pattern)
- Half ROM (partial press)
- Letting scapulae round forward at the stretch
- Pushing through the lower back (lifts from seat)
- Going too heavy too fast (machine forgives form, loads accumulate quickly)
**Substitution alternatives** *(ordered by similarity)*: Cluster 1 #9 Bench Press (when free-weight is appropriate + spotter available) · Cluster 2 #34 DB Bench Press · Cluster 2 #36 Push-Up · floor press · landmine press
**Pairing logic**: Pairs with horizontal pull (Cable Row #55, DB Row, Pull-up). Pairs with arm/shoulder isolation. Primary horizontal push option for A1 Reactivator early phases (no spotter required), A6 Postpartum (controlled return to pressing patterns post-clearance), A8 Senior (lower stabilizer demand). NOT a substitute for bench press in trained-user strength programs — different stabilizer profile, less transferable to athletic patterns.
**Goal applicability**: Build muscle (A2) · Sustainable fat loss (A4) · Major weight loss (A5) · General strength (B1) · Strength endurance (B3) · Team sport season prep (C9) · General health maintenance (D1) · Bone density (D4) · Shoulder rehab, Phase 2 (E3) · Return-to-training after extended pause (E7) · Postpartum reconditioning, Phase 2+ (F4) · Menopause-aware training (F5) · Senior fitness (F6) · Arm focus (G2) · Athletic look (G3)

**Sources**: Saeterbakken, A. et al. (2011). The effects of bench press variations in competitive athletes on muscle activity and performance. J Hum Kinet. · Welsch, E. et al. (2005). EMG analysis of pectoralis major and anterior deltoid during the dumbbell bench press. J Strength Cond Res. · Schick, E. et al. (2010). entries.heading: 62. Shoulder Press Machine
entries.content_markdown:
**Movement pattern**: Vertical push (machine, fixed plane)
**Primary**: Anterior deltoid · Lateral deltoid · Triceps
**Secondary**: Upper pectoralis · (minimal core — seated machine removes anti-extension demand)
**Equipment**: Shoulder press machine (plate-loaded or selectorized; converging or fixed-grip variants). *Swaps*: Cluster 1 #12 Overhead Press · Cluster 2 #35 DB Shoulder Press · landmine press · seated dumbbell press
**Unilateral**: No (most machines allow single-arm)
**Difficulty**: Beginner
**Tags**: machine · compound · hypertrophy · low-skill-floor · rehab-applicable · back-supported
**Form cues**:
- Adjust seat so handles align with shoulders at start
- Sit tall, back pressed against pad
- Press to full but not aggressive lockout (do not shrug shoulders into pads)
- Control return, handles to shoulder height
- Brace core, do not push through the lower back
**Common errors**:
- Seat too low (handles start too high, shoulder strain at lockout)
- Letting shoulders shrug toward ears at lockout
- Half ROM (partial press, especially at the stretch)
- Driving hips forward to assist (defeats machine support)
- Going too heavy too fast
**Substitution alternatives** *(ordered by similarity)*: Cluster 2 #35 DB Shoulder Press (seated) · Cluster 1 #12 Overhead Press (when free-weight standing is appropriate) · landmine press · Cluster 2 #34 DB Bench Press incline (alternative angle when overhead is contraindicated)
**Pairing logic**: Pairs with vertical pull (Lat Pulldown #54, Pull-up). Pairs with arm work. Primary vertical-press option for A1 Reactivator early phases, A6 Postpartum (controlled overhead reintroduction post-clearance), A8 Senior (back-supported reduces core anti-extension demand), E3 Shoulder rehab Phase 3 (controlled overhead reintroduction per protocol). Not a substitute for standing overhead press in trained-user programs — different core and stabilizer profile.
**Goal applicability**: Build muscle (A2) · General strength (B1) · Strength endurance (B3) · Team sport season prep (C9) · General health maintenance (D1) · Bone density (D4) · Shoulder rehab, Phase 3 (E3) · Return-to-training after extended pause (E7) · Postpartum reconditioning, Phase 2+ (F4) · Menopause-aware training (F5) · Senior fitness (F6) · Arm focus (G2) · Athletic look (G3) · Posture/desk-worker rebalancing (G4)
